name: Binary error-correcting codes of length 17 and distance 6
description: Construct the largest set of 17-bit words with pairwise Hamming distance at least 6, the extremal quantity A_2(17,6). Brouwer's table lists 258..340: the lower bound is Milshtein's 2019 nonlinear code, the upper bound comes from semidefinite programming. The 256-word linear reference is the [18,9,6] extended quadratic-residue code shortened by one coordinate; the seed has 32 words.

sources.locator: Gijswijt, Mittelmann and Schrijver: definition of A(n,d) and semidefinite upper bounds.
Brouwer's table, n=17, d=6: 258..340 (lower bound Milshtein 2019), inspected 2026-09-20.

execution.interface: construct() -> nonempty list of distinct integers in [0, 2**N). Each integer encodes one N-bit binary codeword, including leading zeros. Every pair must have Hamming distance at least MINIMUM_DISTANCE. Linear and nonlinear codes are allowed. Score: number of codewords, maximized.

limitations: The 256-word reference is verified in tests by shortening the extended quadratic-residue code; the 258-word record is not reproduced here.
A code larger than 258 words would be a new lower bound and needs independent verification against current tables.
